html:
Kahlil Gibran was a Lebanese American writer, poet and painter, born in Bsharri in the mountains of Lebanon in 1883. His book The Prophet (1923) has sold millions of copies and been translated into many languages.

His family emigrated to Boston in 1895, part of the great Lebanese emigration. He wrote first in Arabic, where his prose poems and stories helped to modernise Arabic writing, and then in English. With other writers in New York he founded the Pen League, a centre of the Nahda, the Arab literary revival.

The Prophet, sayings on love, work and death, was popular with the youth of the 1960s and is read at weddings everywhere. He died in New York in 1931 and is buried in Bsharri, near the cedars.
